body:
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/31588
Mirror issue: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/issues/2222

## What I found

The prepared `main` base already contains the production correction described by the report. `HybridSWAPoolConfigurator` resolves `eagle_draft_num_layers`, adds every draft layer to its per-token coefficient, and uses the combined target-plus-draft cost for automatic sizing. I therefore did not duplicate or alter production sizing logic.

## What changed

- Added an issue-specific regression using a 65.45 GiB budget, eight EAGLE draft layers, SWA ratio 0.1, and page size 128.
- The regression reconstructs the old target-only heuristic and demonstrates that its target fits while target plus eight draft layers exceeds the budget; the checked-out implementation remains within budget.
- Added an independent page-alignment boundary case.
- Added the required investigation report and retained raw issue, test, lint, and GPU evidence.

## Reproduction / validation

```bash
/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-82b29c89343f/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py
```

Result: 43 passed, 7 subtests passed.

Repository pre-commit hooks passed for the changed files, including ruff lint/format, codespell, AST validation, and registered-test validation.

A single assigned AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 ran an independent PyTorch/ROCm FP32 matmul compared with a CPU FP64-derived reference (max absolute error `2.288818359375e-05`). This verifies GPU execution only and is not evidence for the reported NVIDIA serving configuration.

## Limitations

The 8x NVIDIA B300 TP8 host and Inkling-NVFP4 weights were unavailable. I did not reproduce full server startup, the CUDA allocation sequence, FP4/MXFP8 behavior, semantic accuracy, or the multi-node/multi-GPU workload. No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable. The direct prepared-interpreter `python -m ruff` command was unavailable, but the repository-managed ruff pre-commit hooks passed.
